scenes.title: Cold open
narration: Around 95% of mosh pit circle pits rotate counter-clockwise, a spatial anomaly directly correlated with the human population's overwhelming right-hand preference.
This is moshing. Late 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: moshing · United States · Late 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Moshing originated in the southern California hardcore punk scene, particularly Huntington Beach and Long Beach around 1978, evolving from the 1970s English pogo.
Through the 1980s, it spread to Washington, D.C., Boston, and New York, where cross-pollination with heavy metal gave rise to the term 'mosh' via bands like Stormtroopers of Death and Anthrax.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Occurs during live music performances as a form of passionate fan feedback, release of energy, and underground cultural expression, though it has also been viewed by some as a manifestation of aggressive bullying.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Participants push, slam, or run into each other inside a mosh pit.

Variations include the Huntington Beach Strut (strutting in a circle while swinging arms), the Wall of Death (two halves of the audience charging at each other), circle pits (running counter-clockwise in a circle), and hardcore dancing (two-stepping, floorpunching, and windmilling).
Watch for Huntington Beach Strut, Wall of Death, Two-step.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Mike Marine (credited with the Huntington Beach Strut), H.R. of Bad Brains, Scott Ian and Billy Milano of Stormtroopers of Death, and artists associated with its mainstream spread like Billy Corgan and Travis Scott.

Variants include the Huntington Beach Strut in Southern California, Boston thrash and pig piles in Boston, New York hardcore style, psychobilly wrecking, and hip-hop pits which tend to feature jumping in unison rather than violent slamming.
Directly descended from the 1970s English punk pogo, subsequently branching into regional hardcore styles, heavy metal moshing, grunge pits, and modern hip-hop raging.
